Intestinal Abscess, Abdominal Abscess, Carbuncles and Boils (Continued, Lower Section)

When there is hidden, dull pain in the region of Tianshu [acupoint], it pertains to the Large Intestine; when it pertains to the Small Intestine, there is slight pain arising — this indicates the formation of an abscess.

When the Small Intestine develops an abscess (intestinal abscess), the disease presents with swelling of the lower abdomen, aversion to pressure, hardness of the body's flesh. When it becomes large, a red discoloration appears, indicating impending abscess formation.

In intestinal abscess, there is sweating at times; the disease is characterized by fever and abdominal distension; there may be binding below, or pus, or the skin surface becomes rough like fish scales; urination is frequent and scanty, resembling [other conditions].

In intestinal abscess with discharge, or when there are signs of pus in the peritoneal cavity, the mass is large; if pus drains downward, it is appropriate to nourish the blood to promote healing; if the abdominal skin is tense and urgent, abdominal abscess is indicated; [appropriate formulas] should be added accordingly.

For Large Intestine abscess with pus forming within, the pulse of intestinal abscess or forming abscess is flooding and tight — it is appropriate to use the Four Substances Decoction with Rhubarb (Siwu Dahuang Tang); the red swelling will heal on its own.

For damp-heat patterns: use Honeysuckle, Forsythia, Cyperus, Corydalis, and the formulas below; when the pulse of forming abscess is faint, flooding, and tight, use the Small and Equal Decoction (Xiaojun Tang) with modifications for body pain.

For five types of painful urination: use Peach Kernel, Atractylodes, Magnolia Bark; for托裏散 (Interior-Supporting Powder), use the Large Rhubarb Urgent-Press Decoction or Xiaojun Tang with modifications.

For hot urination with Yin membrane involvement: use Cyperus, Moutan Bark Powder, and Interior-Supporting Powder with skin [herbs], thirty [doses], using the Urgent-Press Decoction.

For cases without significant heat: use Moutan Bark Powder and Interior-Supporting Powder with the press decoction.

Poria is appropriate; if the lower abdomen has formed [an abscess], use Moutan Paste, Chengqi Decoction; Rhubarb with Dispersing Powder added as fever subsides.

For established intestinal abscess with cold and yellow [signs], Moutan formula, Peach Kernel Chengqi Decoction — remove and purge.

Pulse Diagnosis Methods

In cases of carbuncles and abscesses that are difficult to differentiate, one can determine the condition by examining the pulse. A flooding and rapid pulse indicates the possibility of intestinal abscess. A slow and tight pulse suggests heat has not yet descended — this is appropriate for intestinal abscess. The Jueyang pulse being slippery and descending, and the Ying (nutritive) pulse being slippery, indicates intestinal abscess. When both slippery and rapid, it pertains to the Wei (defensive) pulse — slippery and rapid with descending Ying pulse indicates heat in the intestinal abscess. When slippery and rapid together, coming from heat and accumulation, it forms an abscess; it is not appropriate to purge when the Wei pulse is slippery and descending.

When the pulse is full and rapid, heat and stagnation are present in the Ying layer, and rapid pulse indicates heat intestinal abscess.

Turbid blood in the upper vessels is drawn to the collaterals below.

**Dahuang Mudan Decoction** — Treats intestinal abscess. When the pulse is slow and tight and pus has not yet formed, purgation is appropriate. Use Peach Kernel (Taoren); if Trichosanthes (Gualou) is unavailable and no pus has formed, apply the powder. Also known by one name including Mirabilite (Xiao). One packet: decoct in half a cup of water and take orally. If Coix seed (Dongwuren) is used and Trichosanthes is unavailable with no pus, apply the powder. Another formula uses Dahuang and Mudan, with Coix seed, each in equal halves.

For needling with blood, use half a coin's weight. Another name: Dahuang Mudan, one packet decocted in water and taken orally, with Coix seed; if Trichosanthes is unavailable and no pus is present, apply the powder.

**Sanren Decoction** — Treats pain in the intestines with abscess. For intermittent cases, one may take Coix seed, Peach Kernel, and Moutan Bark, two qian each.

Right: slice and divide into three portions — Coix seed decoction, Coix seed two and a half qian, Peach Kernel and Moutan Bark each [two qian].

One measure, named Yi Bai (Coix), decocted in water and taken orally.

Modan Powder (牡丹散): Treats intestinal abscess (腸癰). It causes the abdomen to soften and relieves pain; at times there is discharge of pus and blood. Ingredients include moutan bark (牡丹皮), Chinese angelica (當歸), angelica dahurica (白芷), each in the prescribed amounts; poria (白茯苓), astragalus (黃芪), coix seed (苡仁), each two and a half qian; and crushed charred paper (黑破紙), morning glory seed (牽牛子).

Baejangsam Powder (敗醬散): Treats intestinal abscess. The body has no [external signs]; apply a poultice to the abdomen and decoct. Ingredients: aconite (附子), blast-processed until fully cooked, five fen; [other ingredients in stated amounts]. Boil with water, take two qian per dose; administer half dose at a time. Small amounts of ginger.

Byeon-gang Powder (便薑散): Named for [its action on] the lower abdomen; addresses blood and pus from intestinal abscess. Take two liang, reduce to powder; add two liang of rhubarb (大黃) and ox [gallstone/ingredient], reduce to powder, four qian per application; apply with charred black paper and morning glory seed.

Yellow-Black Powder (黃黑散): Treats intestinal abscess, internal abdominal [abscess], bezoar (牛黃) one liang, grind to powder; two liang reduced to four qian per application; apply with charred black paper and morning glory seed.

Treatment Verification for Intestinal Abscess: Take one dose [of the formula], apply topically; [the patient experienced] abdominal pain, which calmed; the abscess resolved. Administer daily as a paste applied to the abdomen and stomach area to draw out the pus and relieve the painful abscess, using the warming formula.

Treatment Verification for Intestinal Abscess (second case): With wine, [treat] the liver and neck region; the abscess formed pus in the intestinal tract with abdominal pain; administer the warming formula as pills, two liang per course.

Arm Abscess (臂癰): [Affects] the yang meridian of the spine and hand yang-brightness channel; treat with wine administration; [the condition] resolved after one hundred doses of the hemp-intestine decoction.

Baiji Seungma Decoction (白芷升麻湯): Angelica dahurica (白芷) and realgar (雄黃), each one qian; fresh yellow [herb] and tea, each four qian; forsythia (連翹), each one qian.

Treating Carbuncles (Yong-Carbuncle Section)

Topical application: Red flower, Platycodon (Balloon flower root), each 5 fen — slice, divide into 2 doses, add water and decoct each portion halfway down. This addresses blood stasis in the yin region; such cases are rare. The middle passage of the yin region tends to be slow to heal.

For scrofulous swellings (luoli): can be sewn closed to protect the channels; there is hardening and swelling; use qi-regulating methods to seek out the affected vessels.

When the lesion burrows, use decoctions internally; track the qi movement to disperse and identify the heat; relieve swelling; for those with deficient and weak qi, after the lesion appears use herbs to nourish and supplement the deficiency; apply moxibustion again.

For urinary tract carbuncle: the physician examines the patient sitting; when the toxin burrows inward and the swelling is painful, it is appropriate to treat internally; afterward, add flavoring to the decoction to harmonize.

When large yellow pus comes out, it is difficult and painful; malignant and hard to treat; the skin turns red.

For sudden perianal carbuncle in the passage: take water with herbs, wrap in fine silk floss and insert into the lower part of the body; check daily.

To treat swelling: it is appropriate to take Guolao Gao (Licorice paste), break it open with a lancet, and gradually the carbuncle will subside. It resembles a lotus seed in growth; ten or more channels form externally, beginning from the scrotal region between.

The initial outbreak occurs in the passage as described before; afterward a large carbuncle forms, called a "bulging carbuncle" (peng-luoli); this disease produces ten or more tracts from the passage; afterward it is difficult to treat; the skin turns red.

Suspended Carbuncle (Xuan Yong)

National Elder Paste (Guo Lao Gao)

[Right column, heading section:]
National Elder Paste: Immediately treats and moistens carbuncles, welling-abscesses, and scrofula. One thousand doses before [meals]. The water — finely ground — invest [the herbs]: suddenly the swelling disperses. Add water, bring to a boil again, take [the decoction], wait — slowly, slowly watch. Sweeten to taste, drink at will. Penetrates through [to the affected area].

[Day by day, afterward, one must take two doses, dispel it three times. If anyone has this carbuncle and it has already broken, take two liang, apply the plaster, and the sore immediately disperses. Drink two or three [doses] to resolve it.]

Convenience Carbuncle (Bian Yong)

Its common name is "Bian Du" (Groin Toxin). Either it first forms a sore and then erupts, or pus and blood appear [directly]. It follows the Yin meridian — one name for it is "Riding Horse Carbuncle" (Qi Ma Yong). Its channel pathway is unusual, for it follows the Ren [Conception] vessel blood channel, and the disease erupts in the region between the inner thigh and groin, with swelling and pain. It is appropriate to purge and drain the toxin. It originates at the root, not in the upper abdomen, not in the hip crease area, but in the lower abdomen...

[Further passage:] The symptom: sometimes there is accumulation, with a pre-existing carbuncle sore from which pus erupts; it is appropriate to drain and purge the toxin. It originates not above the abdomen, but in the region of the lower abdomen below the inguinal crease...

[Column on wrapping herbs inside:] Wrap the medicine inside — for those [with this condition] — apply the medicinal paper patch to the toxin site. Also: Convenience Carbuncle grows in the lower abdomen and inguinal region...

Add Huangqi [Astragalus], resolve swelling and pain, disperse [the toxin] — left and right, both sides — use Tong Qi San (Qi-Moving Powder), Dong Jin San, and the Five Steal Carbuncle [formula]; it is appropriate to use Xue Suan Fang (Garlic Formula) and Xian Tie [Immortal Plaster].

Formulas: Huoming Da Yin Jia [Rescue Life Major Drink, modified], Cheng Jie Nei Xiao San (Interior-Dispersing Powder), Huang Men San.

Formulas: Zhuang Yi Da Huang Tang (Zhuangyi Rhubarb Decoction), Jin Nei Xiao San (Gold Interior-Dispersing Powder), Huang Hei San (Yellow-Black Powder), Wu Xiang Lian Qiao Tang (Five Fragrance Forsythia Decoction).

Recipes for Clearing Toxins: Wangchok Powder

Wangchok Powder (Royal Candle Powder), a wondrous remedy. For initial-stage hidden toxin (便毒), take three large centipedes (蜈蚣)...

[For swelling resembling a finger:] Apply to the affected large area; take with warm wine, to be swallowed smoothly; use mountain water with cinnabar, taken together after grinding, to smear over the swelling; then apply a three-inch adhesive plaster with vinegar; also fresh ginger...

[For dispersing toxin accumulation:] The patient applies fine-ground [herb] steeped in warm wine; take with cinnabar dissolved in the same preparation, applied over the abscess; seal with a three-inch plaster soaked in vinegar; also fresh ginger...

Suhyangsan (蘇方散) — Sappanwood Powder

For treating constipation, carbuncles, Honeysuckle (金銀花), Angelica root (當歸), pangolin scales (山甲), scorpion tail (尾), red peony (赤藥), Sappanwood (蘇木), licorice (甘草), Chuanxiong (川芎), each eight portions, Typhonium (射)...

[Method:] Halve the dose, decoct and take one packet; combine with [herb], right side broken, each one qian, half portion of licorice, one dose...

Oyster Shell and Rhubarb Decoction (牡蠣大黃湯)

For one-sided toxin: Gleditsia pod, ginger, apricot kernel, licorice, each one qian; Gleditsia pod, three fen; Honeysuckle flower; decoct and take one portion with Saposhnikovia (防Wind)...

Detoxifying Drink (消毒飲)

For one-sided toxin: Rhubarb (大黃), Trichosanthes (瓜), three days to resolve the swelling; Gleditsia, each one qian three fen; Honeysuckle flower; decoct one portion with Saposhnikovia...

Wangchok Powder (王燭散)

Apply topically; take with water and wine; Rhubarb (大黃) with immediate effect; each one qian; decoct one packet; with Chuanxiong (川芎) and Angelica (當歸), red...

Take on an empty stomach. For one-sided toxin: Fresh rehmannia (生地黃), licorice (甘草), mirabilite (硝), each one qian; decoct one packet in water; red [peony]...

Miraculous Powder (Shenqi San): Treats swollen toxic sores, fish-mouth sores, swellings, and parotid abscesses. Ingredients: Pangolin scales (Shanjia) 3 liang; the above two ingredients ground; Coptis (Huanglian), Scutellaria (Huangqin), Gardenia seeds (Zhizi), Honeysuckle flower (Jinyinhua), Forsythia (Lianqiao), Oyster shell (Muli) — 1 qian and a half each, all dry-fried; decoct each separately; blend with toad venom (chansu); Cinnamon (Gui) — prepared plain.

Double-Release Powder (Shuangjie San): Take with a small boy's urine, five pieces; used to treat toxicity, promoting large bowel movement; Peach kernel (Taoren), Black ox-knee (Hei chou) — 1 qian each; Licorice powder; 7 portions each; stir-fry; Official Cinnamon (Guiguan) — one portion.

Scrotal Abscess (Nang Yong): This condition arises from damp-heat. It forms along the urinary tract; water accumulates in the yin passage, or injection is needed. Charcoal powder is applied along the tract when urination is difficult. Apply it to the scrotum; double the pus. The pus and qi within the sac flow smoothly inward. Naturally, the condition will spread and gather. The purple color breaks open; tilt the leaves upward. Use purple sac herb (zicang cai); liver; can be used together.

Bone Abscess (Fugu Ju): Oil moistens but does not cure; if left untreated, it leads to death. Use carbuncle-filling method; attach to the affected area; apply internally. Dry, though hard to treat externally — the pus has not yet discharged. Apply skin wrapping with nine-heat method; cover with fragrant herbs eight times; roast at the joints; pass through the channels and joints.

[Further text describes:] Pain deep within, draining, bone fragments emerging, healing occurring naturally. This is a single pus-type disease, but shallow in presentation. It travels to the bone; flying corpse (fei shi) condition causes pain and pressure at the joints, but treatment brings no benefit. It resembles White Tiger Joint Pain (Baihu li jie feng) in pattern. The skin is naturally [treated] with roasting and fragrant herbs at the joints, and the channels are passed through.

Deep-seated abscesses that are entirely painless at first may appear the same to the ear, but they arise initially on the bone, within the sinews and bones; the pain is mixed, and although needling externally and applying heat, one must change and stimulate, making heat arise within to disperse and dissolve. Next, one uses [the formula] to cleanse internally. At first it moves; one then uses fasting internally, next uses a drink. It is in this [condition that it] dissolves below; one sees the toxin dispersed and dissolved. The flesh and muscle show signs of loosening; one sees that internally the coolness and cold cannot transform. Use fire-salt-wing-formula broth to cleanse. See the Primary Vitality Broth to enliven the formula. The bone-born dispersing formula is marvelous for treating stone abscesses — apply green [medicine] extensively. Apply to the sore three times to level the flesh. Use red powder, bright primary broth. Attached-bone powder with red paste should be used to cut away the exterior remainder. When the color is no longer improving, in the intestines and exterior, the kidney organ should be connected. Fang Ji (防已) after prolonged use, while Licorice (甘草) regulates flesh, and the treatment categories oppose each other.

Differentiation of Slow Abscess (緩疽), Stone Abscess (石疽), and Bandit Wind (賊風):
Slow abscess is chronic throughout.
Stone abscess accumulates and is entirely solid.
After days, heat does not harmonize with qi, and they do not blend together, eventually [lodging] between bones.
Like stone, regulate this.
If stone [accumulation], use Shang Lu (商陸) root, pound together with salt using only a small amount, fill in, and apply to the hardened skin between [bones].

After days of solidity that does not harmonize, it lodges between bones like stone — regulate it.
Change the dressing daily; when it becomes soft and cold, the stone abscess arises from wind striking the bone marrow, so the pain also manifests and is lost.

Jujube and Kudzu [decoction], warm [in nature], transforms cold so that the slow abscess arises; one should take Yue Ju Tang (越疽湯) to disperse and unblock, and take tonifying-deficiency [formulas] with flowers.

Methods for Prevention at First Onset

When a condition first arises and treatment proves ineffective, apply a plaster to the designated acupoint (the jumping/tender point) where the pain does not cease. To prevent the development of bone abscess (附骨疽), urgently use two or three doses of Aconite (附子) and other herbs.

Have the patient strip bare, place them above a pit dug in the ground, burn a fire below to make the pit hot and red, so that the heat and steam rise up to cure the stagnant blood.

When the steaming qi brings about a cure, the bleeding will stop.

Loulu Drink (漏蘆飲子)

Treats bone abscess (附骨疽) at its initial onset. Loulu (漏蘆) is the appropriate medicine. It can also be used for early-stage abscesses in other locations. Ingredients: Bai Lian (白斂), Huang Qi (黃蓍), Ma Huang (麻黃), Zhi Shi (枳實), Sheng Ma (升麻), Chi Shao (赤芍), Pu Xiao (朴硝), Gan Cao (甘草) half qian, Da Huang (大黃), Sheng Ma (升麻), Dang Gui (當歸).

Internal Dispersing Shengma Decoction (內消升麻湯)

Decoct and take. Treats bone abscess arising at the foot Shaoyang and Yangming channels. Ingredients: Dang Gui (當歸), Huang Qi (黃蓍), Chi Shao (赤芍), Da Huang (大黃), Sheng Ma (升麻), Gan Cao (甘草), and others in various proportions.

Qianghuo Fangji Decoction (羌活防己湯)

Treats bone abscess arising at various locations. Ingredients: Cang Zhu (蒼朮), Fang Ji (防己), Mu Xiang (木香), Chuan Xiong (川芎), Mu Tong (木通), Jiu Gui (酒歸), She Gan (射干), Bai Shao (白芍), and other herbs in specified proportions.

托裏黃芪湯 (Tuo Li Huang Qi Decoction / Internal Supporting Astragalus Decoction)

Treats bone abscess arising at the foot Shaoyang and Yangming channels. Ingredients: Dang Gui Wei (當歸尾) 1 qian 7 fen, Chai Hu (柴胡) 1 qian, Bai Zhi (白芷) 1 qian 2 fen, Lian Qiao (連翹) 7 fen, and other herbs.

Toad Ointment (蟾蜍膏)
Ingredients: Licorice (甘草), Forsythia (連翹), Toad fat (蟾脂), Rush (蔺), Crow's dipper (烏豆), cook together in a decoction for a long time until the color turns red and the preparation dries. Take one toad, break it open, soak in rice-washing water to remove impurities, then wrap in mulberry bark with oil, wrap in oil-soaked paper, remove from the fire. Use lard, combine with the prepared fat from four liang, decoct and take one sheng orally.
Cardamom (肉桂), Scutellaria (黃芩), each one and a half qian; decoct, serve orally.
Five portions (分) each of the ingredients: one bottle. Apply to sores on the mouth; rub on the sores. The difference is it sticks like glue. Test by applying it afterwards; first with mulberry bark oil wrap. Soak in rice water and remove the dried herb.

Red Atractylodes Pill (赤朮元)
Grind to powder, stir-fry red pepper (赤椒), white angelica (白芷), star anise (大茴香) one liang, one piece broken and soaked in rice-washing water to remove impurities. Make honey pills the size of phoenix tree seeds (梧桐子). Take 100 pills. The above ingredients: grind into fragrant powder with cyperus (香附子).

Muscle-Smoothing Powder (平肌散)
Grind to powder, add light powder (輕粉), mix into a paste, apply to the mouth sores. Over time it heals completely — a proven remedy. Mix with warm wine and withdraw. White bark powder one qian, scorpion two and a half fen.

Three Raw Ingredients Powder (三生散)
For damp sores and emaciation: equal portions of the above ingredients, also roast, preserve the nature as powder. Each dose take three qian, adjust with warm wine. Apply externally; a proven remedy, mix with warm wine.

Green Herb Atractylodes and Phellodendron Decoction (青草蒼柏湯)
Herbal nodes attached: five fen portions; Atractylodes (蒼朮) as appropriate for prevention; each three qian of bark; one and a half qian. Right side cut as one dose, with licorice (甘草) one.

Flow-Injection Bone Abscess (Liu Zhu Gu Ju)

Add cinnamon twig, decoct with water, summer with ginger juice — this is a second formula for deficiency of the body. Take on an empty stomach. In winter, or when there is a chronic swelling with a fixed mass, it is appropriate to add achyranthes root. Or if the condition is due to invasion of wind-cold pathogen, the flow-injection moves to settle at a location; in such cases, add [the appropriate herbs].

When the disease arises or flares up repeatedly, it tends to affect the four limbs or the six fu organs; the eyes may show puffy swelling, the qi and joints are involved. For chronic swelling, take bamboo sap to lead [the medicine] and use scallion to reach [the affected area].

If the patient has spontaneous recurring illness, after pus forms for a long time without resolving, the taste [of the pus changes]; it is appropriate to use a combined decoction, using fermented soybean cake as a warm compress, or with the ointment applied cold; if there is toxin with heat, use four needles to lance the kidney-back, shin, spine-head, and bone-marrow abscess areas.

Where stagnation accumulates and then forms clusters — these are flow-injection abscesses. They spread, forming pus channels that eventually drain.

The flow-injection may cause swelling of the lumbar region and legs, redness and swelling of the hands and feet; accumulating dampness-swelling that does not break, or painful heat, hard as stone, may form in the flesh; or there may be bloody discharge.

Where there is pus between the skin and flesh appearing like purple fluid; wrapped in tissue it may feel soft or irregular, not hard, or on breaking it has a curved and puffy appearance.

Where there is abscess without blood discharged, between the skin and flesh; the texture is like an egg, the main treatment involves the flesh; pus may emerge from the bone; when it softens and moves and is lanced, it should not harden again, or on breaking it curves inward again.

Where there is no proper pus defense, the blood and fluid between the flesh layers resembles a chicken egg; it can move when pressed, soft but not hard; when broken it again shows a curved swollen appearance.

When purple coloring appears at the bone attachment and the abscess discharges at the muscle surface, water and pus accumulate in a fixed form attached to the bone; once it discharges, the patient recovers and the body returns to normal with the bone intact.

Yeongwi Banghon-tang (Decoction for Restoring Vitality to the Nutritive and Defensive Qi)

[Right margin column:] Once a hardened swelling in the yin regions has ulcerated and does not heal for a long time, one should disperse cold pathogenic qi and tonify. Apply moxa using an aconite (fuzi) cake, or apply a warm compress of green onion (scallion) to the affected area.

[Main text:] This formula governs all types of carbuncles and abscesses, cold toxin sores, red scabies, and swellings. It also treats [various named conditions]. Use Mutong (Akebia stem) for swellings.

[Ingredient and preparation notes:] Add Heshouwu (Polygonum multiflorum). Also known as Heshouwu San. Add Rattan [Caulis], Flos Lonicerae (honeysuckle), promoting the flow of qi. Add Fuzi (aconite), Zirантong (native copper), to activate blood, relax sinews, and regulate the flesh. For the interval between doses, use ten winds dispersing formula. For the Half-summer (Banxia) internal formula — where there is hardness and deficiency — add Chuanxiong and Fuzi, pass through and protect, use Huangqi, Dahuang, unblock and smooth downward flow.

For flowing sores and wandering abscesses along the vessels, spreading to the back and thighs with throbbing: after ulceration, if the sore deteriorates, add flower-soaked preparations with muscle-penetrating herbs. For stiff, stagnant, non-perforating cases, add Chuanxiong, Fuzi, Guanchong, and Pangolin scales (Chuanshanjia).

For cases where the yin and yang [qi] of the disease require tonification, use formulas such as Neibushiyixuan (Internal Supplementing Ten Diffusions). These are not merely harmonizing formulas. The yang qi here depends on blood being vigorous and full to flourish; if blood is insufficient, yang cannot be activated. [Add] Lianqiao (forsythia) to harmonize the yin qi and the blood must be fully replenished so that yang qi is not exhausted.

Carbuncle-Boils (疔疽)

A truly divine and marvelous remedy.

[Description of boils on the top and bottom of the feet, and those on the sides:] These are called the "Four Ding Boils." Their appearance is serious; if not treated urgently, within a hundred days death will follow.

If treated urgently and the black [tissue] is removed, this is called a "red-black soft carbuncle." If left untreated, it will redden greatly and the patient dies.

[Regarding foot boils at the toes:] These are called decay-boils. Initially they appear red like a nail-head, then they spread and suddenly protrude. If the area turns from red to black, it cannot be treated; within a hundred days the patient will die.

[These boils] most often arise from eating — from consuming beef, horse meat, or fowl and game, or spicy and pungent foods. They may also arise from accumulated exposure or from listening to [and contracting conditions near] areas where this disease is present in the world.

[Regarding the nature of these boils:] They are without a fixed form of toxin, yet sometimes appear as a deep red streak along the channels, small but with accumulated discharge — hence they are described according to their shape and location in the world.

Signs and Symptoms of Carbuncle-Boils (疔疽形證):

[These boils cause] great heaviness, as if pressing; there is throat pain, [the patient experiences] chills first, then yellow coloration, sudden heat, and the four limbs become heavy and sunken. The head and complexion change color. At onset there is always itching first, then pain; the eyes blur first [before other symptoms appear].

[If accompanied by] dampness and redness, with the skin rotting as if scorched by fire, there is throat pain, initial chills followed by intense heat, the four limbs become extremely heavy, and the head and complexion change color at onset with itching before pain and eye disturbances first.

The pores feel as if bored through; the muscles and flesh are deeply affected; this is difficult to treat. The [affected area] becomes hard and black, like a nail driven in. The face, tongue, and corners of the mouth become red or black.

[The patient suffers] cold sensations in the limbs, pain, rigidity, and a piercing sensation; alternating chills and fever; the face and tongue become red-black in color.

Methods for Treating Clove Sores (疔疽)

When [the sore] appears dark like a mole, with the area closed and not fully [draining], one must not neglect [treatment] at any moment. Or if there is a sore [with swelling] but no pain and no sensation, one should cauterize with a needle and fire.

If the sore has a root and the toxic sore is attacking, if the side of the heart [chest area] has numbness, no pain, and no sensation, one should pierce it directly with a needle.

When a person has blood stagnation, urgently lance it; in one hundred cases of clove sores, drain the blood toxin downward with the needle. If [the toxin] reaches toward the heart, it can accumulate and cause death. One should lance the heart area with a needle.

Around the margin, [if] a carbuncle contracts and causes blood vessel [obstruction], it is also appropriate to use moxa and needle technique. If there is a carbuncle but no blood visible, use the needle to press and directly needle it.

If [the sore] does not respond to medicine, and the carbuncle contracts, urgently lance it and expel [the toxin]; use the needle to circulate and clear it; apply medicinal paste over it.

[In cases of] burning pain, use strong fire [cautery]; for spreading carbuncle, use needle and iron [instruments]; use flying dragon [formula] and other preparations.

For treatment, use: Huo Ming Dan (Life-Activating Elixir), or powder formulas, or elixirs with charcoal [base]; Huang Tang (Yellow Decoction) powder; needle and iron [instruments]; Nine Transformations Toxin-Clearing [formula]; Flying Dragon formula.

Soul-Calming formulas: Ling Dan (Spirit Elixir), Bao Sheng formula, needle preparations; Nine Transformations Toxin-Clearing formula; Flying Dragon formula.
